look_here_first: Find one complete compound leaf and count leaflet pairs: about 4–8 pairs of oval-to-oblong, softly hairy leaflets, versus the SINGLE pair in S. roemeriana and S. pilosior. Verify velvety upper and lower surfaces and the deep-rooted erect perennial habit; use flowers and mature pods as follow-ups, not yellow alone.

morphology_keys.comparison_training: Perennial, many velvety leaflet pairs, tall bushy habit.

comparisons.key_distinctions: S. roemeriana has only one pair of narrower leaflets. S. pilosior is ALSO a perennial with one pair of BROAD hairy leaflets, not an annual; do not use life history to split it. Chamaecrista has smaller numerous leaflet pairs and a petiolar nectary; confirm genus with flower/fruit.
